body.x: KoreaSoft (CEO Nam Yeon-ji) participated in CES 2024 from January 9th to 12th in Las Vegas, USA.

KoreaSoft integrates AI, IoT, and robotics technologies to manufacture and provide smart farm solutions for mass cultivating edible insects. The company also develops and distributes bio-materials using edible insects. With edible insects gaining popularity as an alternative for addressing population growth, greenhouse gas issues, and food security problems due to their high nutritional and environmental value, KoreaSoft advances towards a sustainable future with the slogan “Save the Earth with Insects.”

The smart farm solution aims to support farms that directly produce and sell edible insects or wish to enhance productivity, efficiency, and stable income. The modular facilities of BugsFarm are easily scalable, ranging from a minimum of 45m² to large-scale factories, catering to diverse demands from individual farms to large-scale leased smart farm complexes, according to the company.

A KoreaSoft spokesperson emphasized, “The edible grasshopper, Gom-beng-i, has high pharmacological value in Korea but is sensitive to environmental changes, resulting in significant variations in harvest and price volatility depending on the season. Therefore, our solution development focused on the stable mass production of Gom-beng-i, which is effective in liver health and blood clotting. Through this, we have achieved standardization and scaling of insect quality, allowing even those without experience in insect cultivation to raise them easily with simple training. The All-care service, covering feed to sales, enhances farm income.”

Additionally, the smart farm utilizes AI, IoT, and robotics technology for real-time monitoring and managing environmental factors such as temperature, humidity, light, and ammonia, allowing automatic control of insect breeding, growth, and harvesting processes.

The spokesperson added that the automated feeding and management system maximizes resource efficiency by providing precise nutrients based on the growth stages through modularized automated feeding processes.

Furthermore, the data analysis and prediction system collects and analyzes data through the cloud, monitoring and predicting the status of insects. Applying big data and artificial intelligence technology optimizes productivity and detects potential issues early on.

KoreaSoft has generated its first commercial revenue from BugsFarm by selling research equipment to universities and national research institutes this year. By the end of the year, the company aims to complete a research production facility in a critical regional autonomous area, performing feed-to-product research. In 2024, KoreaSoft plans to initiate a private supply business targeting insect farming enthusiasts and smart farm facilities in essential regions and expand it to other areas. The goal is to achieve facility sales of KRW 20 billion (USD 16 million) by 2027. The company plans to conduct external investment for facility funding in the first half of next year, purchasing a 10,000m² site in an agricultural-industrial complex and completing the construction of a large-scale factory. The production capacity will be expanded to an annual production of up to 1,000 tons by 2028.

KoreaSoft aims to explore new business opportunities in the edible insect smart farm solution and high-performance bio-materials field at CES 2024. The company is determined to secure a foothold for global market entry, increase brand awareness, and enhance its brand image. The spokesperson expressed their commitment to continuous development, improvement, and international expansion of insect industry leadership through advanced solutions and technologies.

body.x: The Consumer Technology Association (CTA) hosts CES, the world’s largest IT exhibition held annually in Las Vegas, USA, allowing visitors to grasp global trends in the home appliance industry at a glance. AVING News, covering CES for 18 consecutive years, has been reporting CES news worldwide since 2006 and selecting the best innovative products, companies, and technologies through ‘BEST OF CES’ and ‘BEST OF MADE IN KOREA.’ Additionally, through ‘AVING LIVE,’ they deliver real-time CES issues.

Incheon City exhibits at the LVCC North Hall AI·Robotics Zone with the “Incheon/IFEZ Pavilion” and the startup zone, “Eureka Park.” The pavilions include the Incheon Creative Economy Innovation Center and the Incheon Startup Park Joint Pavilion. As part of the pre-event promotion for participating companies from Incheon, the city organized a “Pre-global Media Interview” with Ubergizmo, a global media outlet that covers CES annually.
